The graph above shows the velocity of an object moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis. At time $t=0$ the particle is located at the position $x=1.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=7?$
worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=7$ is equal to its position at $t=0$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [0,7].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(7)=x(0)+{\int }_{0}^{7}v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

We are told that $x(0)=1,$ and we can compute the integral ${\int }_{0}^{7}v(t)\,\text{d}t$ by finding the signed area under the graph from $t=0$ to $t=7.$ Computing the signed area, we get

$$
{\int }_{0}^{7}v(t)\,\text{d}t=4.
$$

Therefore,

$$
x(7)=1+4=5.
$$

So, the position of the particle at $t=7$ is $x=5.$
